opportunities.title: 3 Days: The New Patch Cadence Record (SAP Commerce Cloud Edition)
opportunities.why_now: A critical SAP Commerce Cloud flaw went from disclosure to active exploitation in just 72 hours, with three separate outlets confirming in-the-wild attacks.
opportunities.angle: Breach-clock explainer: timeline graphic from CVE disclosure to first exploit, plus what it means for enterprise patch SLAs

opportunities.title: Microsoft Can't Patch Exchange Because Its AI Broke the Fix
opportunities.why_now: Microsoft is publicly blaming AI tooling for delaying a critical Exchange update with no ETA, a rare admission that undercuts the 'AI speeds up patching' narrative.
opportunities.angle: Irony-driven analysis piece contrasting this with the same week's AI-bug-hunting hype (Zhipu, NIST) — 'AI wrote the bug, AI can't fix it'

opportunities.title: ChainDrop: The npm Worm That Slips Past Every Scanner You Trust
opportunities.why_now: A new self-propagating worm is loose in the npm supply chain and specifically evades standard defenses, a fresh escalation in the ongoing package-ecosystem crisis.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor deep dive: how ChainDrop evades detection, IOCs, and a checklist for auditing CI/CD dependency trees today

opportunities.title: 678,000 vs 2 Million: Inside the French Tax Authority's Breach Math Problem
opportunities.why_now: The French tax authority initially confirmed 678,000 affected individuals days after a crook claimed to be selling 2 million records — the gap itself is the story.
opportunities.angle: Breach-disclosure forensics piece questioning why official counts keep undershooting criminal claims, with a running tally sidebar

opportunities.title: ShieldBreak: The Defender Zero-Day With No Patch and a Very Bad Name
opportunities.why_now: Microsoft is scrambling to patch a zero-day in its own Defender product, a rare case of the security tool itself becoming the attack surface.
opportunities.angle: Rapid-response CVE brief: what ShieldBreak exploits, current mitigations while the patch is pending, and why 'securing the security software' is the next battleground
